title: Preventing Maternal Deaths Act of 2018
official_summary:
Preventing Maternal Deaths Act of 2018

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to reauthorize through FY2023 and revise certain Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) programs that support state and local surveillance of maternal mortality.

Among other changes, the bill authorizes the CDC to support state and tribal maternal mortality review committees. Such committees must collect, analyze, and report specified data relating to pregnancy-associated deaths (i.e., deaths from any cause during, or within one year of, pregnancy) and pregnancy-related deaths (i.e., deaths from any cause during, or within one year of, pregnancy that are related to pregnancy or its management, excluding accidental or incidental causes).

summary.headline: This 2018 law reauthorizes and updates CDC programs that help states and tribes track and review deaths related to pregnancy.
summary.what_it_does: The law amends the Public Health Service Act to extend CDC maternal death surveillance programs through fiscal year 2023. It allows the CDC to support state and tribal maternal mortality review committees. These committees collect, analyze, and report data on deaths from any cause during pregnancy or within one year after, and on deaths that are related to pregnancy or its management.

who_it_affects.how: They can receive CDC support to run maternal mortality review committees and collect and report data on pregnancy-associated and pregnancy-related deaths.
Better tracking of pregnancy-related deaths is intended to inform state and tribal reviews of these cases, though the law itself does not directly change their care or benefits.
They are the groups that collect, analyze, and report the specified data on these deaths.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 21, 2018, with program authorization running through fiscal year 2023.
